question.text: Kavitha, an RTA executive, is processing a bonus issue. Applying the current SEBI rule that bonus securities shall be allotted only in dematerialised form, where the entire shareholder base already holds securities in demat, how must the bonus shares be processed?

answer.text: Bonus shares should be held in a suspense account indefinitely
Shareholders are not entitled to bonus shares and their entitlement lapses
Physical share certificates should be printed and dispatched to shareholders
Bonus shares must be credited only to shareholders' demat accounts, in line with the SEBI mandate that bonus securities are allotted in dematerialised form

explanation.text: The Logic: The current SEBI rule referenced on p.136 of the NISM Series II-A workbook is that bonus securities shall be allotted only in dematerialised form. Where the shareholder base already holds securities in demat, the bonus is credited directly to those demat accounts (option D). Suspense accounts, lapse of entitlement, and printing physical certificates are all contrary to that rule. The Trap: Options A, B and C each contradict the demat-only bonus rule. In the original ambiguous version the stem mentioned "both demat and physical shareholders" and keyed an answer that required physical holders to first convert their existing holdings to demat. That treatment is not stated in p.136 and conflicts with p.74 of the same workbook, which says that if a security holder is holding physical securities, bonus securities against those folios shall mandatorily be issued in physical mode only. Note: The original question was ambiguous because the workbook itself conflicts: p.74 mandates physical-mode bonus for physical folios, while p.136 mandates demat-only allotment, and p.136 does not state that physical holders must first dematerialise. The stem has been reframed to the source-backed scenario where the entire base is already in demat, so the SEBI demat-only rule applies cleanly. Source: NISM Series II-A (RTA Corporate, Oct 2025), p.136.
